newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 30.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
--The government is preparing to make important moves in the market and services as part of efforts for full deregulation and help economy and inflation on its course.
--The Bank of Greece will announce its currency policy goals by Monday at the latest. The main focus is expected to be the upkeep of anti-inflationary policies and the support of the 'hard drachma'.
--Ionian Bank has announced two new loans for businessmen: The loans offer low fixed-interest rates of 13.0 percent and are destined for purchase of business premises or movable assets.
--Both Greek and foreign interest has been expressed in the buyout of the 'Epirus' feta cheese industry, sources say. The sale is being coordinated by Citibank.
--New car insurance premiums are expected to go up by as much as 50 percent. Preiums on other insurance products range from increases of 20-40 percent over last year's prices.

--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou is trying to spread the message that prices on the market should be restrained in the interests of lower inflation. Inflation for January is expected at 6.0-7.1 percent.
--The finance ministry dropped interest rates on Treasury buills yesterday from 11.1 percent to 10.9, a decision bolstered by inflation's downward tendencies.
--A new bill on development and taxation incentives, designed to boost investment growth, is being prepared by the national economy and finance ministries.

--Farmers in Thessaly are prepared today to block the Athens-Thessaloniki rail link, upping the ante in their second round of protests. Yesterday, Agriculture Minister Stephanos Tzoumakas received a 'rousing reception' from farmers as he arrived to inaugurate the Agrotica trade fair in Thessaloniki.
--The rise of the dollar has created problems for those taking out loans in foreign exchange.
--Olympic Catering looks to return to state control, sources say.

--Tax incentives for growth are being extended to all small islands as part of efforts to increase investment in private and public sectors and to create jobs. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
